papers.title: Exact Sampling from Determinantal Point Processes
papers.abstract: Determinantal point processes (DPPs) are an important concept in random matrix theory and combinatorics. They have also recently attracted interest in the study of numerical methods for machine learning, as they offer an elegant "missing link" between independent Monte Carlo sampling and deterministic evaluation on regular grids, applicable to a general set of spaces. This is helpful whenever an algorithm explores to reduce uncertainty, such as in active learning, Bayesian optimization, reinforcement learning, and marginalization in graphical models. To draw samples from a DPP in practice, existing literature focuses on approximate schemes of low cost, or comparably inefficient exact algorithms like rejection sampling. We point out that, for many settings of relevance to machine learning, it is also possible to draw exact samples from DPPs on continuous domains. We start from an intuitive example on the real line, which is then generalized to multivariate real vector spaces. We also compare to previously studied approximations, showing that exact sampling, despite higher cost, can be preferable where precision is needed.

papers.title: Joint Sparsity-Based ISAR Imaging for Micromotion Targets
papers.abstract: The micromotion of a target will introduce additional frequency modulations on the radar echoes and lead to a contaminated inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) image of the main body. In this letter, a novel ISAR imaging method is proposed for micromotion targets based on the joint sparsity of the main body spectrogram. Under the sparse Bayesian framework, we assign hierarchical priors to the spectrogram to statistically promote the joint sparsity of the main body signals and eliminate the interference of the micromotion counterparts. To avoid the intractability of calculating the posterior, we utilize the Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling in the Bayesian inference. Based on the approximate posterior, the main body spectrogram is estimated from the samples, and a clear image of the main body can be achieved by cross compression. Imaging results of the echoes generated using both the point-scattering model and the electromagnetic computation have validated the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers.title: A Parallel Controlled Study of the Effectiveness of a Partially Flipped Organic Chemistry Course on Student Performance, Perceptions, and Course Completion
papers.abstract: Organic chemistry is very challenging to many students pursuing science careers. Flipping the classroom presents an opportunity to significantly improve student success by increasing active learning, which research shows is highly beneficial to student learning. However, flipping an entire course may seem too daunting or an instructor may simply choose to use this approach selectively. This exploratory, mixed-methods study examines the effectiveness of a partially flipped course in the first semester organic chemistry course. Two sections were taught by the author in Fall 2015: a control section (n = 28 students) using a lecture-based format, and a flipped section (n = 26 students), where 8, 75 min classes (a third of the course) were taught with flipped pedagogy. Significant improvements in test questions on flipped topics were observed, as well as a significant reduction in the course withdrawal rate. While the average overall course grade was similar in the two sections, the flipped section had 25% more A’s and B’s. Survey and focus group data show that by the end of the semester students in the flipped section felt significantly more confident with the course material than the control section. As measured by student surveys over the course of the semester, students in the flipped section showed a significant change in their preferred type of instruction from lecture to a more collaborative approach, and also showed a significant increase in their comfort level with working in groups and using active learning strategies.

papers.title: Dosage effects of extracorporeal shockwave therapy in early hip necrosis
papers.abstract: This study investigated the effects of different dosages of extracorporeal shockwave therapy (ESWT) in early osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH). Thirty-three patients (42 hips) were randomly divided into three groups. Group A (10 patients with 16 hips) received 2000 impulses of ESWT at 24 Kv to the affected hip. Group B (11 patients with 14 hips) and Group C (12 patients with 12 hips) received 4000 and 6000 impulses of ESWT respectively. The evaluations included clinical assessment, radiographs, dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI for microcirculation (Ktrans) and plasma volume (Vp), and blood tests for biomarker analysis (NO3, VEGF, BMP-2, osteocalcin, TNF-α, IL-6, substance P, CGRP, DKK-1 and IGF). Significant differences of pain and Harris hip scores were noticed between Group A and C in 6 months after ESWT (all P < 0.05). The pain score decreased, but not Harris hip score improved over the observation time period from 6 to 24 months. Total hip arthroplasty was performed in 3 patients (4 hips) in Group A, but none in Groups B and C. Group C showed significant changes in serum biomarkers for angiogenesis, osteogenesis, anti-inflammation, pain threshold and tissue regeneration between one week and one month after treatment (all P < 0.05). However, no significant changes in the infarction volume in image studies were noted in all groups (all P > 0.05). The post-treatment Ktrans and Vp in the peri-necrotic areas of Group B and C were significantly greater than pre-treatment data (both P < 0.05). High dosage ESWT is more effective in early stage ONFH. The systemic beneficial effects of ESWT may ultimately enhance angiogenesis with improvement of microcirculation of the peri-necrotic areas, that in turn, can improve subchondral bone remodeling and prevent femoral head collapse.

papers.title: A Monte Carlo study of ionic transport in a simple cubic random alloy via the interstitialcy mechanism: effects of non-collinear and direct interstitial jumps
papers.abstract: Self-diffusion and ionic conduction via the interstitialcy mechanism in a simple cubic, binary random alloy AB were investigated as a function of composition using Monte Carlo simulation. It was found that allowance for non-collinear jumps (partly) replacing concurrent collinear site exchanges leads to a reduction in diffusion correlation effects. This goes along with a shift of the diffusion percolation threshold to lower concentrations of the (more) mobile component B. Even stronger changes of mass and charge transport compared to an exclusively collinear interstitialcy scheme are observed for additional contributions of direct interstitial jumps. It is remarkable that for both extensions of interstitialcy mediated diffusion, the Haven ratio appears to be greater than unity in certain composition ranges poor in B. All results rely on the calculation of tracer and interstitialcy correlation factors in the simplest possible three-dimensional lattice structure. Yet they may have more general relevance to the interpretation of tracer self-diffusion data and ionic conductivity measurements on crystalline materials.

papers.abstract: Many neophyte researchers such as those who undertake a substantial masters thesis or embark on doctoral research find themselves faced with an unexpected sense of alienation, aloneness and self doubt. papers.title: Who Renews? Who Leaves? Identifying Customer Churn in a Telecom Company Using Big Data Techniques
papers.abstract: Within the context of the telecom industry, this teaching case is an active learning analytics exercise to help students build hands-on expertise on how to utilize Big Data to solve a business problem. Particularly, the case utilizes an analytics method to help develop a customer retention strategy to mitigate against an increasing customer churn problem in a telecom company. Traditionally, the forecast of customer churn uses various demographic and cell phone usage data. Big Data techniques permit a much finer granularity in the prediction of churn by analyzing specific activities a customer undertakes before churning. The authors help students to understand how data from customer interactions with the company through multiple channels can be combined to create a “session.” Subsequently, the authors demonstrate the use of effective visualization to identify the most relevant paths to customer churn. The Teradata Aster Big Data platform is used in developing this case study.

papers.title: Pengaruh Lingkungan Keluarga dan Motivasi Belajar terhadap Hasil Belajar Siswa Kelas X Bidang Keahlian Administrasi Perkantoran SMK Negeri 2 Blitar
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Ratnaningrum, Elok Winda. Pengaruh Lingkungan Keluarga dan Motivasi Belajar terhadap Hasil Belajar Siswa Kelas X Bidang Keahlian Administrasi Perkantoran SMK Negeri 2 Blitar.Skripsi, Jurusan Manajemen, Program Studi S1 Pendidikan Administrasi Perkantoran, Fakultas Ekonomi, Universitas Negeri Malang. Pembimbing: (I) Dr. H. Sutrisno, M.M., (II) Drs.Sarbini.  Kata Kunci: Lingkungan Keluarga,Motivasi Belajar , Hasil Belajar Siswa. Pendidikan mempunyai peranan yang penting dalam mengembangkan potensi yang dimiliki manusia. Pendidikan pada hakekatnya adalah usaha sadar untuk mengembangkan kepribadian dan kemampuan di dalam maupun di luar sekolah serta berlangsung seumur hidup. Penyelenggaraan pendidikan dilaksanakan melalui dua jalur, yaitu jalur pendidikan formal dan jalur pendidikan non formal. Oleh karena itu, pendidikan hendaknya dikelola dengan optimal agar memperoleh hasil yang maksimal. Pencapaian hasil belajar siswa dipengaruhi oleh banyak faktor. Lingkungan belajar dan motivasi belajar merupakan faktor yang mempengaruhi hasil belajar siswa. Lingkungan yang baik dan positif akan berpengaruh baik terhadap hasil belajar siswa. Begitu juga dengan motivasi belajar, semakin tinggi dan positif motivasi belajar yang dimiliki siswa maka akan meningkatkan hasil belajar siswa. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui: (1) Pengaruh lingkungan keluarga terhadap hasil belajar siswa kelas X bidang keahlian Administrasi Perkantoran SMK Negeri 2 Blitar. (2) Pengaruh motivasi belajar terhadap hasil belajar siswa kelas X bidang keahlian Administrasi Perkantoran SMK Negeri 2 Blitar. (3) Pengaruh lingkungan keluarga dan motivasi belajar terhadap hasil belajar siswa kelas X bidang keahlian Administrasi Perkantoran SMK Negeri 2 Blitar. Penelitian ini adalah penelitian kuantitatif dengan menggunakan analisis statistik deskriptif, uji asumsi klasik, dan analisis regresi linier berganda. Variabel bebas dari penelitian ini adalah lingkungan keluarga (X1) dan motivasi belajar (X2) dengan variabel terikatnya adalah hasil belajar (Y). Populasi dalam penelitian ini adalah siswa kelas X bidang keahlian Administrasi Perkantoran SMK Negeri 2 Blitar tahun ajaran 2014/2015 sebanyak 121 siswa dengan sampel yang digunakan sebanyak 94 siswa. Teknik sampling dalam penelitian ini adalah probability sampling dengan jenis proportional random sampling. Instrumen dalam penelitian ini adalah dokumentasi dan kuesioner. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa: (1) Terdapat pengaruh positif dan signifikan lingkungan keluarga terhadap hasil belajar siswa kelas X bidang keahlian Administrasi Perkantoran SMK Negeri 2 Blitar; (2) Motivasi belajar berpengaruh positif dan  signifikan terhadap hasil belajar siswa kelas X bidang keahlian Administrasi Perkantoran SMK Negeri 2 Blitar (3) Terdapat pengaruh positif dan signifikan lingkungan keluarga dan motivasi belajar terhadap hasil belajar siswa kelas X bidang keahlian Administrasi Perkantoran SMK Negeri 2 Blitar Berdasarkan uraian diatas peneliti menyarankan: (1) siswa diharapkan terus meningkatkan motivasi belajar dengan memanfaatkan waktu luang untuk belajar dan memperbaiki diri untuk berkompetisi secara sehat sehingga berpengaruh positif terhadap hasil belajar; (2) guru sebagai pengajar dan pendidik bukan hanya berfungsi untuk menyampaikan ilmu kepada siswa tetapi guru juga harus mampu menciptakan kondisi pembelajaran yang aktif, kreatif, dan menyenangkan agar siswa lebih termotivasi dan tertarik untuk belajar; (3) orang tua siswa agar lebih memberikan perhatian kepada anak-anaknya; (4) sekolah hendaknya menciptakan lingkungan belajar yang kondusif seperti mengatur suasana kelas yang nyaman, menyediakan sarana dan prasarana seperti pengadaan bank mini, perpustakaan yang dilengkapi dengan buku – buku yang relevan, laboratorium, serta ruang praktek ABSTRACT Ratnaningrum, Elok Winda. Influence of Family Environment and Motivation Study on Yield Class X Student Affairs Office Administration SMK Negeri 2 Blitar.Thesis, Department of Management, S1 Studies Office Administration Education, Faculty of Economics, University of Malang. Supervisor: (I) Dr. H. Sutrisno, M.M., (II) Drs.Sarbini. Keywords: Family Environment, Motivation, Learning Outcomes. Education plays an important role in developing the potential of the human being. Education is essentially a conscious effort to develop the personality and ability inside and outside the school, and lasts a lifetime. The education system is implemented through two lines, namely, formal education and non-formal education channels. Therefore, education should be managed optimally in order to obtain maximum results. Student achievement is influenced by many factors. The learning environment and learning motivation are factors that affect student learning outcomes. Good environment and will positively affect both the student learning outcomes. So also with the motivation to learn, the higher and positive learning motivation of the students will improve student learning outcomes. This study aims to determine: (1) The influence of family environment on the results of class X student of expertise Administration SMK Negeri 2 Blitar. (2) Effect of motivation to learn the results of class X student of expertise Administration SMK Negeri 2 Blitar. (3) The influence of family environment and motivation to learn the results of class X student of expertise Administration SMK Negeri 2 Blitar. This study is a quantitative study using descriptive statistical analysis, the classical assumption test and multiple linear regression analysis. The independent variable of this research is the family environment (X1) and learning motivation (X2) with the dependent variable is the learning outcomes (Y). The population in this study were students of class X of Office Administration expertise SMK Negeri 2 Blitar 2014/2015 school year as many as 121 students with sample used as many as 94 students. Sampling in this study is a type of proportional probability sampling with random sampling. Instruments in this study is documentation and Questionnaire. The results showed that: (1) There is a positive and significant influence of family environment on the results of class X student of expertise Administration SMK Negeri 2 Blitar (2) Motivation to learn positive and significant effect on the results of class X student of expertise Administrative SMK Negeri 2 Blitar (3) There is a positive and significant influence of family environment and motivation to students of class X of Office Administration expertise SMK Negeri 2 Blitar. Based on the description above authors suggested: (1) the student is expected to continue to increase motivation to learn by utilizing the free time to study and improve themselves to compete in a healthy manner so that a positive effect on learning outcomes; (2) the teacher as teachers and educators not only serves to convey knowledge to students but teachers should also be able to create the conditions of active learning, creative, and fun so that students are more motivated and keen to learn; (3) parents of students in order to further increase in giving attention to their children; (4) the school should create a conducive learning environment as set atmosphere comfortable classrooms, provide infrastructure and facilities such as the procurement of mini bank, a library equipped with books - books that are relevant, laboratories, as well as practice space
